pr.title: coverage: Split out counter increment sites from BCB node/edge counters

analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation is emitting coverage counter-increment statements by iterating the BCB-node and BCB-edge counter-association maps, conflating "which BCB/edge owns a counter/expression" with "where a unique counter increment must be injected". Once two nodes or edges share the same `CounterId`, that association-driven iteration injects the same counter increment multiple times (unwanted duplicate `CounterIncrement` statements), corrupting counter values. The corrected transformation instead iterates a distinct `counter_increment_sites: IndexVec<CounterId, CounterIncrementSite>` so each counter ID has exactly one injection site, and handles `ExpressionUsed` separately via `bcb_nodes_with_coverage_expressions`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR coverage instrumentation over a BCB coverage graph where counters may be shared by more than one BCB node or control-flow edge. Includes BCB nodes with coverage spans (expressions eligible for `ExpressionUsed`), BCB edges (never have spans), and counters/expressions with and without incoming edge counters.
analysis.originalLogic: Before the patch, `CoverageCounters` allocated fresh IDs via `next_counter`/`next_counter_id` and stored `BcbCounter::{Counter{id}, Expression{id}}` directly in `bcb_counters` (nodes) and `bcb_edge_counters` (edges). Injection in `inject_coverage_statements` iterated `coverage_counters.bcb_node_counters()` and `coverage_counters.bcb_edge_counters()`, and for each entry decided whether to inject: for nodes, `Counter` always injected at `basic_coverage_blocks[bcb].leader_bb()`, `Expression` injected as `ExpressionUsed` only when `bcb_has_coverage_spans(bcb)`; for edges, `Counter` injected into a new block via `inject_edge_counter_basic_block`, while edge `Expression` was never injected.
pitfalls: Do not inject one CounterIncrement per BCB association; inject exactly one per unique counter increment site.
Do not let shared counters cause duplicate counter increments; counter identity and injection site must be separable.
Only inject ExpressionUsed for expressions directly associated with BCB nodes that have coverage spans; BCB-edge expressions never have mappings and must not get statements.
`num_counters()` must reflect the number of increment sites (`counter_increment_sites.len()`), not a monotonically advanced next-ID counter.

If the edge-counter map is iterated in the future, keep deterministic ordering (`FxIndexMap`) to avoid query stability hazards; with the new design the map is `FxHashMap` only because it is not iterated.
Creating an edge counter increment requires a new MIR basic block between the two BCBs; node counters use the leader block directly.
preconditions: Coverage instrumentation is enabled and a BCB coverage graph with counter/expression assignments is being processed.
A counter ID can be associated with more than one BCB node/edge, or the code path injects statements by iterating per-BCB association maps.
Node counters are injected at the BCB leader block; edge counters require inserting a new MIR basic block between `from_bcb.last_bb()` and `to_bcb.leader_bb()`.
Only BCB nodes (not edges) can have coverage spans and thus `ExpressionUsed` statements.
analysis.summary: Decouple coverage counter-increment injection sites from BCB node/edge counter associations. Counter IDs are allocated by pushing a CounterIncrementSite (Node{bcb} or Edge{from_bcb,to_bcb}) into an IndexVec, and MIR injection iterates that site list rather than iterating per-BCB node/edge maps. This allows two coverage-graph nodes/edges to share a counter without emitting duplicate CounterIncrement statements; expression-used statements are handled separately and only for BCB nodes with coverage spans.
analysis.testStrategy: Construct two compiler-input programs that differ only in whether two coverage-graph nodes/edges are made to share a counter (versus each receiving distinct counters), then inspect coverage instrumentation output/MIR dumps: the shared-counter variant must contain exactly one `CounterIncrement` for the shared counter/site, not one per associated BCB. Also test a BCB node with a counter expression and coverage spans gets an `ExpressionUsed`, a node expression without spans does not, and an edge expression never gets a statement. Avoid claiming runtime reproduction; this patch provides no execution evidence.
analysis.trigger: Triggered when counter allocation assigns the same coverage counter to two or more BCB nodes/edges, or when an implementation ties MIR injection directly to per-BCB counter map entries instead of unique increment sites. Also relevant when changing edge-counter storage/iteration, because iteration order can affect emitted MIR/query stability.
